translationRepairs: On yiwei, former Anzhou commissioner Liu Suining became Left Martial Guard general; Binzhou commissioner Jiao Jixun became Right Martial Guard general; and former Yongxing commissioner Zhao Zan became Left Valiant Cavalry general.

On yiwei, former Anzhou commissioner Liu Suining became Left Martial Guard general; Fuzhou commissioner Jiao Jixun became Right Martial Guard general; and former Yongxing commissioner Zhao Zan became Left Valiant Cavalry general.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
Yougui had been acting commander at Yongxing; when Zhao Siyun's revolt broke out he lost the city, and only now was he punished for it.
Yougui had been acting commander at Yongxing; when Zhao Siyun made his sudden assault he lost the city, and only now was he punished for it.
奔沖 describes Zhao Siyun's assault or rush on the city, not merely the outbreak of a revolt.
On renshen, Liu Ci moved from Huazhou to Xingzhou, Yang Xin from Anzhou to Binzhou, and Wang Lingwen from Beizhou to Anzhou, each with an enlarged fief.
On renshen, Liu Ci moved from Huazhou to Xingzhou, Yang Xin from Anzhou to Fuzhou, and Wang Lingwen from Beizhou to Anzhou, each with an enlarged fief.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
On day renshen, Liu Ci of Huazhou was transferred to Xingzhou, Yang Xin of Anzhou to Binzhou, and Wang Lingwen of Beizhou to Anzhou; all received enlarged fiefs.
On day renshen, Liu Ci of Huazhou was transferred to Xingzhou, Yang Xin of Anzhou to Fuzhou, and Wang Lingwen of Beizhou to Anzhou; all received enlarged fiefs.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
Binzhou acting commissioner Wang Rao became Huazhou commissioner in reward for attending court.
Fuzhou acting commissioner Wang Rao became Huazhou commissioner in reward for attending court.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
Wang Rao, acting commissioner of Binzhou, was made military commissioner of Huazhou because he had come to court.
Wang Rao, acting commissioner of Fuzhou, was made military commissioner of Huazhou because he had come to court.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
On bingwu the emperor's brother Liu Xun, Xingyuan commissioner, was named Kaifeng mayor and vice grand councilor but had not yet left the palace.
On bingwu the emperor's brother Liu Chengxun, Xingyuan commissioner, was named Kaifeng mayor and concurrent Zhongshu Ling but had not yet left the palace.
The emperor's younger brother is Liu Chengxun, and 兼中書令 grants the concurrent title Zhongshu Ling rather than Vice Grand Councilor.

On day bingwu, the emperor's younger brother, Liu Xun, commissioner of Xingyuan and imperial envoy, was made mayor of Kaifeng and additionally Vice Grand Councilor, but had not yet left the inner quarters.
On day bingwu, the emperor's younger brother Chengxun, commissioner of Xingyuan, was made mayor of Kaifeng and additionally Zhongshu Ling, but had not yet left the inner quarters.
The emperor's younger brother is Chengxun; the text's 承使勛 reflects a corruption of 節度使承勛, not a man named Liu Xun or an additional imperial-envoy office.
On xinwei an edict sent palace-guard foot commander Wang Yin to encamp at Chunzhou.
On xinwei an edict sent palace-guard foot commander Wang Yin to encamp at Chanzhou.
澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.
Xuzhou inspector Ma Duo reported commissioner Liu Xin had committed suicide.
Xu Prefecture inspector Ma Duo reported that military commissioner Liu Xin had committed suicide.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, distinct from Xuzhou (徐州). Rendering the administrative unit in English is clearer than a parenthetical character gloss.
